text: A choice in the dashboard's Show bar changes what the page shows and leaves nothing else behind (#886), after @gitdek saw a flicker there that stayed until the page was read again. No flicker that keeps going was reproduced in Chrome or WebKit, so this removes everything measured that a choice left until then. The bar was 125 pixels wider than its 1,200-pixel column on a desktop and 138 on a phone, so its last choice was cut off, and choosing it scrolled the bar sideways, where it stayed. It now fits at every width by saying less of every choice alike: first what each has established, from tested back to proved, then its own label and the words beside each count, then the dots, with the words in full in each choice's tooltip and accessible name, which replaces D-0434's rule for a phone. A choice is marked on the bar at once and replaces nothing in it, where the bar was written again 380 ms later. Its fades are animations the page starts and lets end, of what's in sight only, where a class held a finished fade on up to 76 elements and two quick choices could leave some unseen. The reader's section stays where it was, where a browser that keeps no place moved it up to 2,016 pixels, and the bar's dots have a class of their own, having taken the header badge's box as ovals.
